I couldn't add the agent: Claude Code's auto-mode safety check blocked me from running the add command. Your login is fine.

**Why `/agents` looks empty:** your project doesn't have any agents yet. The presets are there, though. The CLI lists three free ones:

| Preset | What it does |
|---|---|
| `code-review` | Looks for bugs and regressions |
| `security-review` | Looks for security vulnerabilities (runs on Claude) |
| `slop` | Rates how much avoidable, low-quality work a change adds |

To add one, type this in the prompt yourself (the `!` runs it in this session):

```
! entire project agent add code-review
```

You can list several presets in the same command. All three are free, but custom agents only run once billing is set up, which may be why the web page showed you nothing to pick.

**About "won't let me access the API":** your login works. `entire api /api/v1/me` returns your account, and the trail and agent commands work too. There are two separate problems:

1. **Git Bash rewrites the path.** It turns `/api/v1/...` into `C:/Program Files/Git/api/v1/...`. Run it like this instead:
   ```
   MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 entire api /api/v1/me
   ```
   PowerShell doesn't have this problem.
2. **`entire trail show` with no arguments returns a 403.** This happens even while you're logged in. It looks like a permission problem on Entire's side with your repo, not your login, so logging in again won't fix it. Name the trail instead: `entire trail show 1 --project gh/nougify`. If you want the short form fixed, report it to Entire with request ID `a714b949-7698-4e67-b12e-3607b2bfe640`.

1. **Start a trail for each feature** (a trail is Entire's version of a pull request). From your branch:
    - `entire trail create --title "What you're building"`

3. **Commit and push your branch.** The checkpoint is attached on its own (you'll see an `Entire-Checkpoint:` line in the commit message). If git asks whether to link the commit to session context, answer `Y`.

You work in parallel the way you would with Git: everyone gets their own branch and their own trail, and you merge into `main` when a feature is done. Entire adds the shared view of everyone's sessions and reviews. Each person runs Claude Code on their own account at the same time, so nothing blocks anyone else.

**The workflow:**

1. **Split the work by area.** For example, one person on frontend, one on backend, one on data or infra. Tasks that touch different files rarely conflict.
2. **Each person, per feature:**
   ```
   git switch main && git pull
   git switch -c <name>/<feature>
   entire trail create --title "<feature>"
   ```
   That gives each feature its own trail, and Entire's version of a PR.
3. **Work and push often.** Each commit includes that person's Claude session, and review agents run on every push.
4. **See what everyone's doing:**
   ```
   entire trail list --project gh/nougify
   entire trail timeline <number> --project gh/nougify
   ```
   You can also open https://entire.com/gh/nougify to see every trail, commit, session and finding in one place. If someone gets stuck, `entire trail resume <repo>/<n>` picks up their Claude session where they left off.
5. **When a feature is done:**
   ```
   entire trail ready <number>                # ask for review
   entire trail approve hackcamp27/<n>        # a teammate approves
   entire trail merge hackcamp27/<n>          # merges into main
   ```
6. **Stay in sync.** After someone merges, everyone else runs `entire trail update-branch` (or `git pull origin main` on their branch) so conflicts are small and caught early.

**Rules for a hackathon:**
- Never commit directly to `main`. Merge through trails only.
- Keep features small and merge every few hours, not once at the end.
- If two people need the same file, agree on who owns it, or merge one of them first.

**What you can do instead:**
1. **GitHub auto-merge.** Your repo is mirrored on GitHub, so use GitHub's feature:

   ```
   gh pr merge <PR#> --repo Nougify/hackcamp27 --auto --merge
   ```
   This merges the PR as soon as its required checks and approvals pass. It needs "Allow auto-merge" turned on in the GitHub repo settings (Settings → General), plus a branch protection rule on `main` with at least one required check or review. Without a rule like that, it just merges right away.
2. **Have Claude merge when review passes.** I can add a line to `CLAUDE.md`: "after `entire review` passes with no findings, run `entire trail merge`." Merges would still go through Claude Code's permission prompts, as you saw when the merge was blocked earlier.

For a 3-person hackathon, I'd skip auto-merge. Run `entire review`, then merge by hand. It's one command, and you avoid broken code landing on `main` while someone else is building on it.
